definitions.explanation: A humble way to refer to one's own husband when speaking to others. This is the traditional term used when women speak about their own husbands.
The master or owner of a household, business, or establishment.

examples.japanese: {主人|しゅじん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。

examples.english: That shop's taste changed after the owner changed. It was more delicious before.

notes:
{主人|しゅじん} is a humble term traditionally used by wives to refer to their own husbands. It literally means 'master,' which some modern speakers find hierarchical.

KEIGO:
- {主人|しゅじん}: my husband (humble, about one's own)
- ご{主人|しゅじん}: your/someone's husband (respectful)

MODERN ALTERNATIVES:
Some women prefer ⟦{夫|おっと}→{夫|おっと}：00982_otto⟧ (neutral) or ⟦{旦那|だんな}→{旦那|だんな}：12330_danna⟧ (casual) instead. {主人|しゅじん} remains common but is sometimes debated for its hierarchical connotation.

SENSE 2 - OWNER/MASTER:
Also means the owner or proprietor of a shop, inn, or establishment: ⟦{店|みせ}→{店|みせ}：00497_mise⟧の{主人|しゅじん} (shop owner), ⟦{旅館|りょかん}→{旅館|りょかん}：01049_ryokan⟧の{主人|しゅじん} (inn owner).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{夫|おっと}→{夫|おっと}：00982_otto⟧: husband (neutral, official)
- ⟦{旦那|だんな}→{旦那|だんな}：12330_danna⟧: husband (casual); also master/patron
